content_raw: {"idea": "Occlusion gradients: treat a fixed batch of `noul` content probes as a continuous readout function of the STATE text — p = f(S) ∈ [0,1]^k — then take finite differences over span deletions/insertions to get a free input Jacobian ∂p/∂S. Outputs a per-span saliency ranking and a robustness margin (greedy smallest set of deletions that flips any probe across 0.5), computed with zero labels and zero logprob access.", "mechanism": "1) Fix ~16 `noul` content probes (e.g. 'state indicates a price', 'state indicates cancellation', 'state contains a date') with identical `instructions` every call; prose-level only, no same-entity/identity questions, so subject-key routing is untouched. 2) Baseline: one batched call — 16 questions, one API call, ~1/12 the cost of per-question. 3) Sentence-segment the state into m spans; for each span i, one batched call with S\\\\span_i → p_i. 4) g_i = ||p_i − p0||_2, signed per-probe Δ as well; rank spans by g. 5) Margin readout: reuse the per-span deltas as a priority queue and greedily delete until any probe crosses 0.5; each additional greedy step costs exactly one batched call, so margin is ~m + 2 calls per record total. 6) Cross-model validity check: recompute g on jev-preview for the top-3 spans only (3 extra calls) and measure rank agreement with jev-latest — agreement means the gradient is a property of the record, disagreement means it is a model quirk. 7) Optional refinement: split top-ranked spans into token-level halves and repeat (log2 calls) for a sub-sentence boundary.", "cheapest_falsifier": "Noise-floor test first, since answer-layer wobble is already measured: run the identical batch twice on the same record (2 calls) to get the same-input delta distribution sigma; then run one real span deletion (1 call). If every span's ||Δp|| sits inside ~2·sigma — i.e. deletion signal never exceeds the identical-input wobble — the idea dies for ~4 API calls per record. If it clears the floor: 6 records × 6 spans = 6 baseline + 36 deletion calls + a 12-call random-span control, and the falsifier becomes whether the deletion curve (top-k spans removed) beats the shuffled-span curve at dropping p, or AUROC of the ranking vs. a held-out diagnostic span ≈ 0.5. Also falsified if top-3 rank agreement between jev-latest and jev-preview is at chance.", "why_novel": "Every prior use of the question map has been output-space: a batch (cost), a routing key (identity), a cross-exam (adjudication), or an embedding (E-Q21 labels). This reframes it as a continuous differentiable-ish readout of the input — the thing `noul` probabilities buy that a discrete `choice` answer structurally cannot — turning a closed, logprob-less API into an attribution engine with no gradients, no labels, and no second system: input saliency and an edit-distance-to-decision-boundary margin, which is exactly the diagnostic you need before trusting any downstream decision on a record, and which nothing in the E-Q21 embedding path exposes (embeddings show similarity, not which sentence bought the conclusion)."}

{"idea": "Coherence deficit: treat one batched systemone call not as N independent answers but as a single joint distribution, emit a question map that closes a small Boolean algebra over two claims from the record (A, not-A, B, not-B, A and B, A and not-B, not-A and B, not-A and not-B, A or B), then measure the norm of the probability axioms it violates in that same response — a free per-record scalar that no per-question confidence can see.", "mechanism": "Per subject-keyed record, pick claims A and B from the existing claim set. POST /v1/systemone with one 9-entry typed map (all noul, instructions phrased so each yields p(yes)) covering the atoms and marginals over {A,B}. Because all nine go out in one call, the returned probabilities are assigned jointly in one pass rather than as nine independent samples — which is exactly what makes axiom-checking meaningful. From that response compute R = |pA+p!A-1| + |pB+p!B-1| + |p(A	or B) - (pA + pB - p(A and B))| + |sum of four atoms - 1| + sum of max(0, p(A and B) - pA) + max(0, p(A and B) - pB). Then run four readings: (i) distribution of R across records; (ii) R vs the sealed family label (does a record whose claims are internally muddled produce a larger residual?); (iii) R added as a second feature beside the existing confidence-based grounding score — does the pair lift AUROC over confidence alone; (iv) for half the records, inject one mild internal contradiction into the `state` text while keeping the claims answerable identically, and check whether answers stay put while R spikes — i.e. R as a detector for state that the answers themselves mask. R costs zero marginal tokens: it is computed from the batch the fleet already pays for, and needs no label to compute — labels are used only to evaluate it.", "cheapest_falsifier": "20 records, 1 call each, 9-question map (one evening, roughly 20 x ~2k tokens). Kill it if either: (a) |sum of four atoms - 1| sits under 0.03 for all 20 and R has essentially no variance — the model is trivially self-consistent and there is no signal channel; or (b) R has variance but AUROC vs the sealed label lands inside 0.5 +/- 0.1, and adding R to the existing confidence feature moves AUROC by less than 0.02. A cheaper pre-check on 5 records costs nothing new: if the atom-sum is already perfect to 3 decimals, stop there.", "why_novel": "The fleet has used batched typed maps for cost/coverage, one-shot per-question confidence as a grounding signal (0.894 vs 0.403), and cross-exam batteries adjudicated over *answers*. None of those treats the batch as one joint distribution or inspects the *relations between* questions rather than the questions themselves. Answer wobble measures instability across runs; coherence deficit measures inconsistency *within* a single run — a different axis entirely. It is also not an answer and not a confidence: it is a constraint-violation norm, self-supervised, computable for free from tokens already billed, and uniquely enabled by the fact that the API lets a whole algebra of related propositions be assigned in one pass."}
